主题玩法就是肉鸽爬塔+类魂，前面几个小关卡体验还算不错，但玩到后边就会发现设计存在很多互相矛盾的地方，四不像 1.[h3] 经验=货币 [/h3] 这游戏经验（鲜血）和货币是挂钩的，所以在这一方面击杀敌人获得的鲜血给得特别少，而商人贩卖的物品又贵又垃圾，光靠每个小关卡给的那几个花苞根本运转不起来 2.[h3] 遗宝唯一 [/h3] 那么多遗宝却只能拿一个，丢了就没了，也不加属性，爬塔最精髓的地方没了，那你设计这个系统是干嘛的呢？ 3.[h3] 难度高，零成长，挫败感强（最关键）[/h3] 因为是类魂游戏，难度高一点也不是不能接受的地方，但问题就在一个大关卡打完需要一个多钟，而中途一旦死亡就前功尽弃，除了那几个少得可怜的解锁武器和开局给得一个召唤外对玩家角色的提升几乎为零。这就导致当你历经艰难终于站到关卡boss前结果被一脚踹死后又得从头再来，成长是没有的，难度是不变的。 [b] 综上所述，游戏主打的类魂+爬塔肉鸽两个类型完全冲突了，数值方面过于小气，想爽又爽不起来。那既然如此想玩类魂的为什么不直接去玩艾尔登法环，想玩肉鸽为什么不去玩Hades。这几个游戏再菜起码都能通过堆游戏时长来完成通关，这游戏只有纯坐牢[/b]

Cool concept but currently I don't know what this game wants to be. Imagine playing Dark Souls or Elden Ring but dealing no damage and enemies being the spongiest thing in gaming history, I don't know if you messed something up when scaling for solo but it's painfully boring to the point where I just let the bosses kill me because it's better than suffering through the nightmare of depleting their health bar. Same goes for most enemies. The upgrades just feel bad, like 90% of them are just ♥♥♥♥♥. Animations are stiff and too strict, it's just doesn't feel good to play. Ordinary sprint is completely pointless, like why have a super sprint? The super sprint is just your typical sprint but you've added a "normal" spring for some reason, why? Because you want to mimmick Nightreign for no reason? The meta progression sucks, there is nothing you unlock progressively by just playing so say I get to the 4 boss and have explored everything up to that point. Well there is nothing else to improve anymore unless I progress past that boss, I'm just wading through the same boring monotony, through the same boring boss fights and boring enemies and boring levels. Obviously the criticism is based on the first early access version here so hopefully it improves. The foundation is perfectly fine except for the really awful animations and general gameplay feel.

Seemingly there are times where iframes do not register properly even when I see my friend get hit or myself, some design choices seem pointless as if they didn't even test their own game and I could probably name an entire list of other stuff that just seems entirely bad. I dont review much but as a small developer seeing a game like this with so much heart and soul i cant help but say its a very well made experience will a very deep system when it comes to character builds. THER ARE SO MANY! PROS: - Very darksouls. Even has shortcuts you can open that stay open forever. So your next run you can use them. - It is very much a roughlike - The dogerolls DO have i frames and you can get abilities that make the I frames longer - Fun solo -Fun with 2 -Fun with 3 - Not a easy game (still have not beat a run) - a massive amount of build types you can do. This includes weapons, characters and all the stat upgrades such as relics and seeds. - Game is full of soul ( What i mean is the game feels like it was made by a team who was really enjoying what they were building) Something that is not very common surprisingly in this industry. - Devs this was super cool of you ! When your in the middle of a run and invite a friend they just pop into your run with you. I was in a run with a friend and a 3rd wanted to join but we had some really fun builds going and didnt want to redo just to bring him. So my buddy invited him as a joke. To our surprise he was put into our game instantly. So cool and just one of those prime examples of soul. Cons: i will not mention anything that is currently being fixed. Any negative comments about glitches are not valid anymore as the devs has updates on steam calling out the issues. - The second boss that looks like a rhino i would really like to see his one attack were he sprints around the map like a train not be so janky looking. Its very still compaired to every other animation and looks like a pinball bouncing around the walls. Im having a very hard time thinking of things because again this is a early access game that is 15$ and theres not much i dont like. I think this game is the bees knees. Try it out

个人浅玩了一下还挺喜欢的，不过还是抢先体验阶段，内容不算太多，快的话五个小时能通关目前两张图。 【优点】 游戏的美术风格和怪物设计、场景设计之类的挺对我胃口，跑图探索挺开心的。 我玩的魂系游戏不多，只狼法环浅玩过一阵，然后还玩了嗜血代码之类的，很讨厌死亡了会掉钱在原地还需要去捡这个设定。这游戏也会看到前几局掉的钱，但具体的机制好像有区别，而且本质上是roguelike所以每局都从零开始，掉了也无所谓，没什么压力，我还是挺喜欢的。 打击感这块我是纯木头，感觉不出好坏，不过本来就是小制作了，这种地方我也不会这么苛责。包括角色动作上、手感上肯定不及大厂和老资历，但是也还过得去，没有特别难受。ui，字体，美术等细节都学得很到位，看着也挺顺眼的，不糙。 【缺点】 然后几个值得吐槽的地方。 1、内容量 这个是肯定的，毕竟是抢先体验。目前的内容量还是较少，两个关卡（每个关卡4层地图，总计8个关内boss）。比较想知道后续正式版的体量大概会是几个关卡。并且有没有稍微具体一点的roadmap，给支持的玩家多一些信息。并且现在boss战斗时的bgm还是较为单一（虽然也很带感），有没有打算未来细化的时候让bgm再多元化一点。 2、boss的设计 这个有些复杂，首先boss的外形上我都还是挺满意的。但是只有[spoiler] 伟大姐妹Vali拥有二阶段，其余都是一阶段 [/spoiler]。这是我没想到的，主要她先出现，让我对后续也有些期待，但是频频落空。其次是这个顺序安排和boss本身的技能设计之类的。个人认为难度最高的是图一的守卫者BATOUSH，相比之下沙丘行者MUHAA有些太简单了，招式较少且技能威胁性不大。梦境看守REZAA招式不少但是钻地太频繁，也不攻击只是转移地点，有些莫名其妙（虽然给了我们救队友的空间）图二因为只打了一次，对boss招式了解程度不深，REDEEMER的招怪有点恶心，第一波刚打完就招第二波了。 3、平衡性和数值 只是浅玩了一下但是感觉还是需要调整。刚开始打的时候觉得挺难的，比较有挑战性，出现变化是在拿到了BATOUSH的锤子之后，选择了合适的职业配合这把武器，伤害直接太高了就莽过去了。我也可以理解总会有轮椅和难用一点的流派，但也希望体验差距不要太大，目前感觉有的流派前期数值太低了，这把锤子又太猛了。然后不知道是BUG还是什么，我大约出现过三次，用BATOUSH锤子释放特殊技能的时候一下子秒杀砸死了血特别高的boss，30%血、55%血、75%血的MUHAA各秒杀了一次，这应该属于恶性bug，需要研究一下是什么情况。 4、时空行者 设计得挺好的我其实内心深处挺喜欢这种东西，有点像虚空怪兽格利扎，但是捏马的冲我过来的时候吓死我了键盘都吓飞了。虽然很喜欢但你们做得也太吓人了点，生理上实在接受不了，所以我看到这个诅咒就会直接退出这局重开。要不你们做个时空行者恐惧症模式？（不用当真） 5、细节和系统 这个遗宝系统我觉得是也可以思考一下还有没有更好的改法，只能带一个，不能额外带，说实话基本都是一整局都用初始的，从头带到尾，boss掉的经常很随机很没用，也只有一个人能替换，商店里卖的也不想换，并且很贵，没什么意义。包括这个货币也是，给的少，东西卖得贵，选择也少，基本就是最后买两瓶药，偶尔买一个种子，钱多了没啥用，完全不打路上的小怪又没经验去升级加点。还有就是每张地图的最终boss打完还会接着掉遗宝，有些意义不明，捡了有啥用吗，然后结尾也都是大蛇，不知道会不会细节上会有什么改动。 总得来说未来可期，希望快快更新，多出一些地图，敌人和boss。推荐和朋友一起玩，魂游爱好者想要当单机玩的话我就未必推荐了，毕竟和市面上那些顶尖单机魂游肯定还是有一定差距，包容度高一点的可以买来玩玩。黑环我也没玩过，不知道这俩算不算一个品类。

There is a select audience that will really enjoy this game, but unfortunately I don't think I am part of that group. I bought this game because I saw many people comparing it to Nightreign with more rougelike elements. Nightreign is one of my favorite games of the last few years, so I was very excited to get a similar experience in another game. Unfortunately, the combat really kills the game for me. It feels like combat you'd expected from a game developed 10-15 years ago. The main issue I have with the combat is that it is pretty slow and methodical, feeling a lot more like Dark Souls I than a more modern and fluid souls-like. Both the character and enemies often feel very clunky and there is often quite a lot of jank with the combat. Enemy attacks are often poorly telegraphed unless you have them memorized, hitboxes often behave very strangely, and often the best strategy for dealing with an enemy is to cheese them by exploiting their bad pathfinding. It really emulates how older souls games almost have turn-taking combat, where you hit an enemy, then they get to hit you so you dodge, then they become open so you hit them. I am sure some of this will get better with time, but I do not see the core, slow combat changing. Since it's a rougelike you can of course bypass this in certain ways by blowing up enemies instantly, but overall this seems to be the core combat design. If you are a big fan of the older Dark Souls games or slow combat you will probably enjoy this game, but if you are looking for something with faster and more fluid combat I don't think this game is for you.

I like it, but I wouldn't recommend it to other people. It is a niche product designed to cater to a tiny subsection of people that are heavily into games of its genre. I've enjoyed a lot of Dark Souls 3, Elden Ring (and Nightreign), but much of what makes those games function does not work in a game like this one. The things that are good are really good, but some of the things that are bad are so baked into the core of the gameplay that I don't think they're something that could be easily changed. For me it boils down to 3 things: 1) Healing Limited healing works in difficult Soulslikes because you return to where you last rested when you die, which means that even when you fail, you are repeating the same section in relatively short order in order to learn how to get through it, and if you feel like you need to run back to recover your health/healing items, you can do that and then use the knowledge you just gained to push further with less healing needed. In Serpent's Gaze, you recover Nectar only between levels or by paying Blood before a boss. Since the only source of non-lifesteal healing is Nectar (or I guess the support class whose healing depends on dealing damage to charge it), that means that the process of learning anything new that's introduced beyond the first stage can be *excruciating*, as you will quickly run out of healing items and die to attrition. It begins to feel as though healing options are must-pick options for upgrades, since that's the only way to counteract the massive cost of a single missed dodge. 2) Run length (This has been patched, so I deleted this part.) 3) Enemy attack patterns Enemies' movements are sudden, and they track quite aggressively. A major criticism back when Dark Souls 2 released was how aggressively enemy attacks tracked the player, such that the *only* option was to i-frame through attacks with dodges. It feels very much the same in Serpent's Gaze, which leads to many enemies feeling like their animations are designed specifically for gap closing and roll catching. The ones that immediately come to mind are the heavy mace knights, the rapier boss, the gatekeeper boss, and the sword/board devotees. They each have attacks that feel as though they were designed by checklist; "We need one attack with a quick windup, and another attack with a longer windup that is delayed by just enough to punish players that roll because they were expecting the other attack. Oh and we need one or two long-range gap closers." I struggle to recall any enemies that are *only* threatening when you get close (they all have aggressive gap-closers or ranged attacks) or enemies that have slow, easy-to-read attacks with lingering hitboxes on their swings, such that you dodge them by positioning rather than i-frames. Eventually you just learn the roll timings, but the answer to every enemy is generally animation reading and memorizing roll timings, which begins to feel stale. ...So overall, while *I* like it, I can't really recommend it for other people, because I find myself going into longwinded explanations about the above-mentioned issues instead of talking about the good parts.

I'd give Serpent's Gays a thumbs up/sideways for trying to look like Tales of Arise, but it's overall just eye candy but not an enjoyable game. Level designer & the post process guy did a decent job. And the little round guy with the big mask is a memorable design. Now, I got this after watching a recommended video claiming it's like Nightreign, without without the circle and time limit. While the latter part is true, it's almost nothing like Nightreign. So I review this with the "Nightreign-Like, But" bias in mind. The combat is a janky Unity-game Asset Pack type of system (even though it's clearly UE5 with all the glorious Temporal Smearing and crashing included), the animation timings are off, sections of the animations are either way too snappy or way too slow for no reason... The music is very underwhelming. You swing twice and dodge, out of stamina... No weapons to pick up. The little passives you pick up seem to just be "add bleed/element damage (over time)." Exploration isn't really a thing, it's just a linear path to follow without any hidden treasure or anything at all to do except run forward and kill the 20 or so enemies before you reach a boss.

How dare you make a Soulslike with no way to permanently increase or grind for better stats. This was billed as a "better, slower paced Nightreign" and it is but a cheap mockery with a Byzantine coat of paint. The combat is deeply unenjoyable due to the hitbox detection; I typically rock strength builds and it is impossible to stagger even the smallest of enemies. Immensely disappointing. The only progression (thus far) is the collection of new weapons or different "classes" which are glorified starting stat allotments. Not great. At least there's coop and it work - I will give it that much credit.

Wish there was a meh/neither option. Its a great idea for a game hands down. but wish the levels weren't so linear and had more reason to explore. The enemies lock onto the player way too hard and almost all of them have gap closers so spacing doesn't overly matter except for a couple enemies. Also their attacks track way too hard, unless you perfectly time every roll you're taking damage due to lack of i-frames, even darksouls isn't this tight for i-frames. There's a lot of builds, that being said only 2 of them seem viable (summoner or healer) Theres no way to save a run and they can take quite a chunk of time to complete. Some weapons feel overly clunky, especially the rapier (Considerings its a finesseful weapon the attack is way too slow and you can rarely get a full combo off before getting hit/running out of stamina) The seeds are a cool feature, however the stats given on quite a few of them don't feel worth taking. Hopefully theres major improvements and balancing as this game is developed, it shows a lot of potential.

Game is gorgeous and exhibits impeccable concepts, but I am very disappointed to say that terrible balancing and design choices make this one of the most frustrating and unrewarding roguelikes I've ever played. Every little thing in this game feels either over- or under-tuned. Level-ups are too infrequent and don't feel nearly impactful enough. Seeds (boons/perks that you get from predestined pickup areas on each stage) are too infrequent and most of them are laughably useless, only increasing things by inconsequential percentages. Enemy health scaling in later stages is very over-tuned. Player power does not keep up with it and late game always feels like a terrible slog unless you get extraordinarily lucky runs. Enemy health scaling is even more of an issue in multiplayer, as scaling is blown way out of proportion. Many of the weapons feel useless compared to others and many weapons' stat scaling is underwhelming. Many of the playable classes feel inconsequential to gameplay. The previous two points create a bit of an identity issue for weapons and classes which otherwise could be very good. Perhaps the most egregious aspect of this game and a testament to how poorly balanced it is is the fact that it is more efficient to skip all enemies on stages 2, 3, and 4 (and possibly the first stage as well if you're competent with bosses and get lucky with seeds) and simply rush for seed pickups, smithing tables for weapon upgrades, and end bosses. This proves that level-ups are largely inconsequential and enemies have far too much health in later stages. This potentially turns a 1 hour 10 minute run on average into a 25 minute run. In short, the majority of the game is not worth it. Pretty dire. Overall, things feel very bland and lacking in any real sauce, which is an absolute shame considering how much this game is positively dripping in atmosphere and potential. I say all of this, again, feeling very disappointed, as this game is GORGEOUS, feels great, is super easy to pick up and play with friends, and has a great soul that only needs to be brought out with a bit more development time. I really want this to be the best it can be, but I feel sad admitting that anymore I'd rather it just be better than it is. I have 1,400+ hours in Nightreign and have no problem winning almost every run at max rank. I can win most runs in Risk of Rain, Dead Cells, and other roguelikes. I cannot say the same for this game, and it's because you simply aren't given the power, the fun, or even the incentive to keep up with over-tuned enemies. I still think it's worth picking up on sale and playing with pals or with randoms in the Discord server and showing it some love in the hopes that it does turn into something great. It's very unique and has potential to be fantastic. I pray the devs will take heed.

HONEST AND TRUTHFUL REVIEW (97.7HRS CLOCKED) AFTER my first 100hrs of playing this game, I can confidently say I was disillusioned. The reason being the fact that I was able to clear the first map due to skipping the third and fourth levels (picking up seeds along the way of course) and, that being said broke my enjoyment of what I had thought was a very fun, invested 1hr-1hr20min run sequence turning into a frenzied 45min run. I could only imagine it's the same for the second map. If I were able to beat the boss without 5-10 possible levels behind, what is the point of continuing to fight the small to large mobs (exception to mini-boss Serpertkin & Planeshifter)? Considering the 'roguelike' aspect of this game, this had not come across my mind due to the fact that I was mesmerized by the 'souls' like aspect of the game but, this in turn made me reconsider putting anymore time into it as for my enjoyment is ruined thanks to this simple trick! Truthfully... I'd wait until this game develops further to play it. Don't buy at the cost of losing/investing precious time into what could possibly might be the best/worst experience of your gaming career. - 3IgChUnGuS out!

No neutral option available but if you can tolerate DS2-again with limited enemy variety, different colored "+2% giggle damage on Tuesdays under the full moon" upgrades, punishing roll-catches, poor telegraphing, excessive enemy tracking, poor communication of damage taken (when, where, and why), no parry mechanic (making blocking pointless), minimal variety/changes in the levels per run (they don't change at all, only the enemy placements do), and just overall being one of the poorer soulslikes available on the market all in exchange for a soulslike game with multiplayer rogue-like elements? Go for it. That's basically the only good thing the game has going for it. The game being this niche in it's appeal just makes it impossible to tell other people to buy. Of note, some abilities just flat out don't work (or don't graphically communicate them working, which is bad) and this applies very badly to NPC tracking/aggro - summons of any type just idle or seem to walk around aimlessly, they don't seek out or function so any abilities that use them is dead in the water. Also the lock on? Horrible. It makes zero effort to lock on to the thing in front of you and instead seems to pick targets with a heavy left-to-right priority instead of proximity to you - every other soulslike I can think of has fixed this or included it as a menu option. Map geometry collision is inconsistent, sometimes you can go over random debris and sometimes it prevents you from moving - the same applies to the arrows on the bridge map, where this is the MOST frustrating. These aren't preference issues, these just straight up don't work. It's still fun though playing with other people, but thats almost INSPITE of the game's many many problems.

The game is good and I intend to play it a lot more in the future. But at the same time, I feel as if it would greatly benefit from the Dungeon layouts and all mobs being randomized every single time (or at the very least pulled from a numerous list of preset dungeon layouts like in TBOI). There are obvious and recurring motifs of a Rougelike (and the game even has a tag for it). I think deaths resetting the progress for each of the two regions (minus the opened gates) is a good addition, but that the game should lean in more heavily into the Rougelike aspect. No two runs should be the same type of deal.

I wish I could vote yes on this, but it just has so many issues. The main problem is that it is a blatant Dark Souls clone, but with no new ideas and far far less content. There's like 10 weapons you can use in this game. Even Dark Souls 1 had dozens and dozens. There were some cool bosses, but all of them were defeated easily. And again, no new ideas there, just inferior bosses to Dark Souls. If you like this kind of game, then just go play Dark Souls 1, 2, 3, Elden Ring, Nightreign, Demon Souls, Bloodborne, and all their DLCs. There is a limitless amount of content that is just flat out better in every way. It's fine to be inspired by a game, but you have to add something of your own to it, do something novel or interesting. This game I beat with my friend in 4.5 hours. There's hardly any content. On top of that, there's hardly anything you could call a "build." Buying this game is like going shopping for a puppy and instead of choosing the several available to you, you grab some roadkill on the street and pretend it's the same thing. It's just worse than what it's imitating in every single conceivable way.

Game has amazing potential, but many poor balancing choices, as well as absolutely infuriating unlock requirements for several things, namely complete RNG. The (arguably) best weapon in the game is unlocked purely via random chance, as is one of the classes. I can understand a super rare and powerful weapon being a rare, random drop, but a class should NEVER be purely random chance. There is no way to weight the RNG, and they aren't tied to any quests or basic requirements. So for unlucky people, such as myself, it's just meaningless to even try. I've unlocked everything else in the game, and now my only option is to mindlessly beat my head against the wall while I pray for pure luck, and instead just get repeated runs of nothing for weeks now. Will update to a positive review when unlocks are not PURELY random chance.

If you like unfair, unbalanced gameplay, this is the game for you. "Normal" monsters are literal pushovers, but they represent about 20-30% of the density in stages. Most of the time you fight "elite" monsters that can only get staggered 2-3 times before being immune to stuns for 10 seconds and don't worry, you won't kill any elites within 2-3 staggers, you will need need at least 20-30 hits to kill them with basically every single weapon in the game. Oh and weapons, what a complete joke they are. In the current 13 weapons in the game, 5 of those are "Ultra" weapons that take so long to swing that virtually EVERY monster in the game can hit you before you land a single hit and guess what, any monster hit staggers you instantly. In the other 7 weapons remaining, 3 of those are "Dexterity" focused weapons that literally do 2-4 damage per hit, guess how many hits you need to kill a boss in this game with those weapons: at least 100 hits for the first boss of the game, THE FIRST BOSS!!! I don't know what is in these dev's smoking pipes but they are clearly on the good stuff. The only time I beat this game in 20 hours of gameplay was with the same build that applies "status effects" like burning, poison or bleeding because the massive amounts of 1-2 damage ticks stack up in the 5-10 minutes of boss fights you are stuck in. How on earth is this game rated as very positive on steam at the time of this review is simply beyond me.
